hindi: इस प्रकार जिसका शल्य निकाल दिया गया हो, उसे गरम जल से सींचे।
english: Thus, her from whom the śalya (dart, foreign body) has been drawn out one should sprinkle with warm water.
notes: Follows the removal of the retained placenta in units 119-120. Śalya (literally a dart) is not defined in the line; the context suggests the retained fetus or placenta, but the text does not say so. The woman is the understood object (feminine accusative nirhṛtaśalyām).

hindi: तब जिसके शरीर पर अभ्यंग किया जा चुका हो, उसे योनि में स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा का पिचु यानी फाहा दे।
english: Then one should give, to her whose body has been anointed, a swab (picu) of sneha (oil or fat) in the yoni (vagina).
notes: The printed snehapicuṃtataḥ is one token: sneha-picum tataḥ. Picu = a swab or pad (of cotton or wool); the material is not stated. Sneha = oil or fat (the kind is not stated).

hindi: उससे योनि मृदु हो जाती है और इसकी पीड़ा शान्त होती है।
english: By that the yoni (vagina) becomes soft, and her pain subsides.
notes: mṛdu is grammatically masculine beside feminine yoni (adjective in a predicate; print and usage allow it). The optative bhavet is rendered as a plain statement of the result. "That" is the swab of unit 122.

words.gloss: rāsnā (Pluchea lanceolata or Alpinia galanga; disputed; on a conjectural reading of printed rāstrā)
the group of five called pañcakolaka (named in note)

hindi: दीप्यक यानी सम्भवतः अजवायन, अतिविषा यानी अतीस, अनुमानित पाठ पर रास्ना जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, हींग, इलायची और पंचकोलक यानी पाँच का समूह।
english: Dīpyaka (probably ajwain), ativiṣā (atis), rāsnā (on a conjectural reading of the printed rāstrā; identity disputed), hiṅgu (asafoetida), elā (small cardamom) and the pañcakolakas (the group of five).

text_flags.why: possible: the drug name is rāsnā; stra for sna is a known confusion in this print (same word in 148)
possible: a stray space; hiṅgu + elā = hiṅgvelā, so the g of hiṅgu sits at the head of the next token

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in unit 125, where the verb (pāyayet) and the forms of administration are given; this unit is only the list of drugs in the accusative. The printed tokens hiṃ | gvelāpaṃcakolakān are hiṅgu + elā + pañcakolakān; the first token carries hiṅgu whole and the "gu" printed at the head of the second token is part of it. Identifications: dīpyaka = ajwain (probable; the older name is also given to other carminative seeds); ativiṣā standard; rāsnā disputed (Pluchea lanceolata in north India, Alpinia galanga in the south); hiṅgu standard; elā standard. Pañcakolaka is a group of five spices; the five are not named in this line (in the Aṣṭāṅga tradition usually pippalī, pippalīmūla, cavya, citraka and śuṇṭhī; probable, not stated here). The plural endings of a list ending in -ān are as printed.

hindi: चूर्ण को स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा के साथ, या कल्क यानी लुगदी, या क्वाथ यानी काढ़ा, उसी प्रकार पिलाए।
english: One should make (her) drink the powder with sneha (oil or fat), or the kalka (paste), or the decoction (kvātha), likewise.

text_flags.why: possible: kvātha (decoction) is meant; the v is missing (also in 130)

notes: The object is the drugs of unit 124 (not repeated here); that "her" is the woman is understood. pāyayet "should make (her) drink" (glossary: open wording). The text does not say which of powder, paste or decoction is preferred.

words.gloss: hiṅgu (asafoetida; on a conjectural reading of printed ghigu)

hindi: कटुका यानी कुटकी, अतिविषा यानी अतीस, पाठा यानी सम्भवतः अकनादि, शाक यानी सम्भवतः सागौन की छाल, अनुमानित पाठ पर हींग और तेजनी जिसकी पहचान विवादित है।
english: Kaṭukā (kutki), ativiṣā (atis), pāṭhā (probably velvetleaf), the bark of śāka (probably teak), hiṅgu (asafoetida, on a conjectural reading of the printed ghigu) and tejanī (identity disputed).

text_flags.why: possible: tvak + hiṅgu gives tvagghiṅgu; the printed ghigu has lost the nasal ṅ

notes: Elliptical list; the verb (pāyayet, unit 125) is carried and not supplied. Compound division is partly ambiguous: śāka-tvak (bark of teak) is taken as one item; the alternative is śāka and tvak (a spice bark, probably cinnamon) as two items. Tejanī: candidates include Zanthoxylum armatum (tejovatī) or other pungent plants; disputed. Kaṭukā standard. Pāṭhā: Cissampelos pareira is the usual identification (probable), others are named by commentators. The compound ends in the accusative plural -īḥ as printed.

words.gloss: doṣa; flowing off; for the purpose of
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. acc. sg. used adverbially

hindi: और उसी प्रकार दोष के बह निकलने के लिए और वेदना की शान्ति के लिए।
english: And likewise, for the flowing off of the doṣa and for the relief of pain.
notes: Gives the purpose of the drugs and forms in units 124-126. doṣasyaṃdārthaṃ is read doṣa-syanda-artham (the flow or discharge of the doṣa; doṣa not specified); the reading is not certain. "Likewise" (tadvat) refers to the way of giving described just before; the line has no verb.

hindi: इस प्रकार तीन रात, सात दिन; तब केवल स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा ही पिए।
english: Thus for three nights, for seven days; then she should drink sneha (oil or fat) alone.
notes: The wording "trirātram evam saptāham" gives two periods side by side with no "or" or "and"; whether they are alternatives (three nights or seven days) or successive is not settled by the line, so none is supplied. The subject (the woman) is understood.

hindi: सायं अरिष्ट यानी खमीर उठाकर बनाया औषधीय पेय पिए, और उसी प्रकार भली-भाँति बनाया हुआ आसव।
english: In the evening she should drink ariṣṭa (a fermented medicinal liquor), and likewise a well-made āsava (also a fermented medicinal liquor).
notes: The doubled k of sukkṛtam is a print habit (normalised in w, recorded here once for the chunk, as are the doubled consonants in vīryyojāṃsi, varddhaṃte, nivarttaṃte, kāśmaryya and arddha). The line does not say which ariṣṭa or āsava. Ariṣṭa and āsava are both fermented herbal preparations (standard).

words.gloss: śirīṣa (siris, Albizia lebbeck; standard); kakubha (arjuna, Terminalia arjuna; standard); decoction; swabs (picu)

hindi: और शिरीष यानी सिरस और ककुभ यानी अर्जुन के काढ़े के पिचु यानी फाहे योनि में रखे।
english: And one should place in the yoni (vagina) swabs (picu) of the decoction of śirīṣa (siris) and kakubha (arjuna).

text_flags.why: possible: kvātha (decoction) with the v lost, as in unit 125

notes: Picu as in unit 122 (swab). The compound can mean swabs soaked in the decoction or swabs of the decoction-drugs; the line gives no more. Kakubha = arjuna (standard).

hindi: और जो अन्य उपद्रव यानी जटिलताएँ हों, उनकी चिकित्सा अपने-अपने अनुसार करे।
english: And whatever other complications (upadrava) there may be, those one should treat each according to its own.
notes: Upadrava = a secondary affliction or complication. "Each according to its own" (yathāsvam): the noun to be supplied is not stated and none is added. Printed ye'nye is ye anye.

hindi: अधिकतर वात को हरने वालों से पकाया हुआ दस दिन भोजन में हितकर है।
english: (What is) cooked mostly with Vāta-removing (ones) is beneficial in the meal for ten days.

text_flags.why: possible: prāyaḥ (for the most part) has lost its long ā; prayaḥ is not a word

notes: Copula "is" supplied; the nouns for "what is cooked" and for the Vāta-removing (ones) are not stated and are shown as (one)/(ones). Printed daśāṃhaṃ is daśa-aham ("for ten days"), accusative of duration.

words.gloss: light; wholesome; little; eating (conjectural reading of printed padvyā)

hindi: और रस दस दिन; उसके बाद अनुमानित पाठ पर हल्का, पथ्य और अल्प भोजन करने वाली।
english: And the rasa (juice) for ten days; thereafter, on a conjectural reading, she who takes light, wholesome and little food.

text_flags.why: possible: padvyā is not a word; pathyā (wholesome) fits the sense and the letters (th/d, y/v confusions occur in this print)

notes: The sentence has no main verb here; it reads as a continuation of unit 132 (diet of the woman). Rasa is the word as printed (juice or essence; the kind, e.g. a meat soup, is not stated and is not supplied). Param can be "thereafter" or "excellent"; "thereafter" fits the ten-day periods. The compound laghu-pathya-alpa-bhojanā is on a conjectural reading as flagged; meaning "eating light, wholesome and small meals".

hindi: स्वेद यानी सेंक और अभ्यंग यानी तेल मालिश में लगी हुई वह बलातैल आदि स्नेहों का सेवन करे।
english: Intent on sweating (sveda) and anointing (abhyaṅga), she should resort to sneha (oils or fats) beginning with balā oil.
notes: The subject "she" comes from the feminine parā (the woman after the ten-day diet). Balātaila is described in unit 137.

hindi: चार महीनों के बाद वह क्रम से और सुखद।
english: After four months, she, gradually, and pleasant (ones).
notes: Elliptical and incomplete: the verb (probably "she should resort to", bhajet from unit 134) is not supplied. sukhāni is an adjective for an unstated noun (neuter plural); it may be a damaged word (compare mukhāni) but nothing in the print marks it; read as printed. ūrdhvam + ablative is taken as "after four months" (open point in the glossary). GROUPING: appears to continue unit 134.

words.gloss: balā (country mallow, Sida cordifolia; standard); oil

hindi: अब हम बलातैल का उपदेश करेंगे।
english: Now we shall teach the balā oil (balātaila).
notes: Opening formula of the recipe in unit 137. Balā = country mallow (standard; the Sida species are also used under this name).

words.gloss: yava (barley, Hordeum vulgare); kola (jujube, Ziziphus jujuba); kulattha (horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum); daśamūla (the ten roots); decoction
unclear (printed form; ends in tailasya, "of oil")
kākolī (identity disputed: Roscoea purpurea or a Fritillaria type)
kṣīrakākolī (identity disputed: Fritillaria roylei or Lilium polyphyllum)
aśvagandhā (ashwagandha, Withania somnifera; standard; on a conjectural reading of printed ahvagandhā)
śatapuṣpā (dill, Anethum sowa, or fennel, Foeniculum vulgare; disputed)
patra (leaf; probably Indian bay leaf, Cinnamomum tamala; probable)
tvak (bark; probably cinnamon, Cinnamomum verum; probable)
sarja (probably the sal tree, Shorea robusta, or its resin; probable)
kālānusārya (unidentified; on a conjectural reading of printed kālānusārthya)
(prefix of anu-guptam, printed with a space)

hindi: बला की जड़ के काढ़े के छह भाग, उतने ही दूध के, यव, कोल यानी बेर, कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी और दशमूल के काढ़े का एक भाग, और अनुमानित पाठ पर तेल का एक भाग जिसकी मात्रा अस्पष्ट है; सबको अनुमानित पाठ पर एक साथ करके, और महीन चूर्ण काकोली, क्षीरकाकोली, जीवक, ऋषभक, मुद्गपर्णी, माषपर्णी, मेदा और महामेदा नामक द्रव्य, क्षीरशुक्ला, मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी, देवदारु यानी देवदार, मंजिष्ठा यानी मजीठ, चन्दन, सारिवा यानी सम्भवतः अनन्तमूल, बला यानी बरियार, तगर, कुष्ठ यानी कूठ, शतावरी, अनुमानित पाठ पर अश्वगन्धा, पुनर्नवा यानी गदहपूर्णा, शतपुष्पा जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, पत्र यानी सम्भवतः तेजपात, त्वक् यानी सम्भवतः दालचीनी, सर्ज यानी सम्भवतः साल, शैलेय यानी सम्भवतः छरीला, वचा यानी बच, अगुरु यानी अगर, अनुमानित पाठ पर कालानुसार्य जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, और सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक डालकर, धीरे-धीरे मृदु अग्नि पर तैयार करके अच्छे पात्र में भली-भाँति सुरक्षित रखे।
english: Six parts of the decoction (kaṣāya) of balā (country mallow) roots, just as many (parts) of milk, one part of the decoction of yava (barley), kola (jujube), kulattha (horse gram) and the ten roots (daśamūla), and, on a conjectural reading, a part of oil whose measure is unclear; having put all that together (on a conjectural reading), and having added the fine powders—kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, mudgaparṇī (probably a wild mung plant), māṣaparṇī (probably a wild urad plant), medā, mahāmedā, kṣīraśuklā, madhuka (probably licorice), devadāru (deodar), mañjiṣṭhā (Indian madder), candana (sandalwood), sārivā (probably Indian sarsaparilla), balā, tagara, kuṣṭha (costus), śatāvarī (wild asparagus), aśvagandhā (ashwagandha, on a conjectural reading of the printed ahvagandhā), punarnavā (hogweed), śatapuṣpā (identity disputed: dill or fennel), patra (leaf, probably Indian bay leaf), tvak (bark, probably cinnamon), sarja (probably sal), śaileya (probably stone-flower lichen), vacā (sweet flag), aguru (agarwood), kālānusārya (on a conjectural reading of the printed kālānusārthya; unidentified) and saindhava (rock salt)—and having prepared (it) slowly over a gentle fire, one should store (it) in a good vessel, well guarded.

text_flags.why: possible: caiturdaśa is not a measure word; probably the measure of the oil is damaged (caturdaśa "fourteen" is one guess). The printed form is kept unsplit; the reading is conjectural
possible: aikaṣṭya is not a word; kya/ṣṭya confusion is known in this print; aikya (union, together) fits
possible: ahva for aśva (śva/hva letter reversal is seen in this print)
possible: th for y; kālānusārya is a known drug name
possible: the print splits anuguptam as 'nu | guptaṃ; kept as printed

notes: Recipe (balātaila). Quantities: six parts of balā-root decoction, as many of milk, then a part of the yava-kola-kulattha-daśamūla decoction, then a measure of oil that is unclear in this print; GROUPING: appears to complete the recipe announced in 136. The "bhāgo bhāgaścaiturdaśatailasya" stretch cannot be restored from the print; no measure is supplied and the translation marks it conjectural. aikaṣṭyaṃ: probable aikyam (together); the translation says so. The big dvandva: the neuter plural ending -āni is shared by all members; ślakṣṇacūrṇāni is taken with it (the list as fine powders); whether the powders are "of" each drug or the drugs themselves are the powders is the same in effect. Identifications (once for the chunk, tags as in the glosses): standard: devadāru, mañjiṣṭhā, candana, kuṣṭha, śatāvarī, aśvagandhā, punarnavā, vacā, aguru, saindhava, balā; probable: mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī, madhuka, sārivā, patra, tvak, sarja, śaileya; disputed: kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka (these four are the aṣṭavarga drugs in later tradition; their group name is not given here), medā, mahāmedā, tagara, śatapuṣpā; unidentified: kṣīraśuklā, kālānusārya. Printed ahva-/arthya- readings are flagged. The avagraha in vacā'guru is a print habit (ā + a). Hindi मेदा always with नामक द्रव्य (glossary). Yava, kola, kulattha: yava barley (standard), kola jujube (standard), kulattha horse gram (standard).

words.gloss: rājamātra (unclear sense; perhaps persons of royal rank)
marma (vital spot); pierced; fallen; struck; broken; dislocated; limbs
divine; injury; cursed; mind; fever; afflicted (conjectural reading)

hindi: यह तैलराज यानी तेलों का राजा, भगवान् धन्वन्तरि को मान्य, राजाओं, राजमात्रों जिस शब्द का अर्थ अस्पष्ट है, कृशों, सूतिकाओं यानी प्रसूताओं, शिशुओं, बीती आयु वालों, सुकुमारों, महाग्रहों से गृहीतों, दीर्घ रोग से क्षीण शरीर वालों, जिनके अंग मर्म में बिंधे, गिरे, आहत, टूटे और उखड़े हों उनके, और अनुमानित पाठ पर दैव उपघात, अभिशाप और मनोज्वर से घिरे हुओं के लिए पान, नावन यानी नाक में डालना, अभ्यंग और बस्ति यानी एनिमा में प्रयोग करने योग्य है।
english: This king of oils, approved by the venerable Dhanvantari, is to be used in drinking, nasal administration (nāvana), anointing and enema (basti) for kings, for rājamātras (a term of unclear sense), for the emaciated, for women recently delivered (sūtikā), for infants, for those past age, for the delicate, for those seized by great graha (seizers), for those whose bodies are wasted by long illness, for those whose limbs are pierced at a marma (vital spot), fallen, struck, broken and dislocated, and, on a conjectural reading, for those afflicted by divine injury, by cursing and by mind-fever (manojvara).

text_flags.why: possible: daivāepaghāta is a garbled daivopaghāta; mamo is probably mano (n/m confusion); the whole compound is a conjectural reading

notes: Dhanvantari is named as the authority; taila-rāja "king of oils" is the recipe of 137 (balātaila). "Rājamātra" is not clearly known (kingly persons, royal kin or an official class have all been suggested; none is certain) and is not translated further. "Atītavayasām" = "of those whose age has gone by", taken as the aged; "past age" is kept literal. "Mahāgrahagṛhīta" = seized by great graha; graha = seizing (seizer), not "seizure". The compound marmaviddha-…-aṅga can also be read as "those pierced at marma, fallen, struck, broken, and those with dislocated limbs"; the division is not fixed by the print. Printed eṣa before bh (visarga dropped by regular sandhi) and dhanvantarer abhi (r-sandhi) are regular. Nāvana = nasal administration (nasya); basti = enema here (the device or bladder sense is not intended).

words.gloss: strength; manly vigour (pauruṣa); memory; understanding; intellect (medhā); digestive fire (agni); vīrya (potency); ojas (vital essence)

pakṣaghāta (hemiplegia, standard); ākṣepaka (convulsive disorder, probable); ardita (facial paralysis, probable); and so on; various; Vāta; disorders; gulma (abdominal lump, probable); hidhmā (hiccup, standard); śvāsa (breathlessness, standard); kāsa (cough, standard)

hindi: उससे बल, पौरुष, स्मृति, मति, मेधा, अग्नि यानी पाचन अग्नि, वीर्य यानी शक्ति और ओज बढ़ते हैं, और पक्षाघात यानी अर्धांग का लकवा, आक्षेपक यानी ऐंठन के दौरे, अर्दित यानी चेहरे का लकवा आदि अनेक प्रकार के वात विकार, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, हिध्मा यानी हिचकी, श्वास यानी साँस की कठिनाई और कास यानी खाँसी दूर होते हैं।
english: By that, strength, manly vigour (pauruṣa), memory, understanding, intellect (medhā), digestive fire (agni), vīrya (potency) and ojas (vital essence) increase, and the various Vāta disorders beginning with pakṣaghāta (hemiplegia), ākṣepaka (convulsive disorder) and ardita (facial paralysis), gulma (abdominal lump), hidhmā (hiccup), śvāsa (breathlessness) and kāsa (cough), cease.
notes: Modern equivalents: pakṣaghāta = hemiplegia (standard); ākṣepaka = convulsive disorder (probable); ardita = facial paralysis of the Bell's palsy type (probable); gulma = abdominal lump or mass (probable, the exact modern entity is not fixed); hidhmā, śvāsa, kāsa standard. The last four are listed in the same clause; the text names them as ceasing in the same clause, it does not say they are Vāta disorders. Doubled consonants (vīryyojāṃsi, varddhaṃte, nivarttaṃte) are print habits. Doṣa Vāta is capitalised.

words.gram: pres. pass. part. upa-√yuj, m./n. inst. sg.

hindi: और प्रतिदिन प्रयोग करने से छह महीने बाद अन्त्रवृद्धि यानी हर्निया शान्त हो जाती है।
english: And, used day after day, antravṛddhi (hernia) subsides after six months.

text_flags.why: possible: the d of the ablative (ṣaṇmāsāt, before a voiced sound) sits at the head of the next token; antra is meant, not dantra

notes: The first token ṣaṇmāsā carries the ablative of ṣaṇmāsa; its final d (ṣaṇmāsād) is printed at the head of daṃtravṛddhiḥ. The ablative of time is rendered "after six months" (it could also be "in six months"). Antravṛddhi is a swelling of the intestine, i.e. hernia (probable). "It" is the balātaila; the pronoun is understood.

words.gloss: by wish, as she wishes (conjectural reading of printed icchyā)

hindi: और बाँझ स्त्री अनुमानित पाठ पर इच्छा के अनुसार गुणवान् पुत्र को पाती है।
english: And a barren woman gets, on a conjectural reading of the printed icchyā, a son possessed of good qualities as she wishes.

text_flags.why: possible: icchyā is not a regular form; icchayā (by wish) fits; icchantī (desiring) is the other possibility

notes: The closing iti marks the end of the statement. Labhata is the regular pre-vowel form of labhate, so no separate flag. Alternative reading: icchantī "desiring" (a woman who wishes for a virtuous son gets one). Vandhyā = barren woman (infertile; standard).

hindi: और इस विषय में ये हैं।
english: And on this matter there are these.

text_flags.why: possible: bhavanti cātra is the usual formula (as in unit 117 of this chapter); ta for ti is a misprint

notes: Standard lead-in formula, "and on this there are (verses)"; the noun is not stated in the Sanskrit and is not supplied. It introduces the verses that follow (143 onward).

words.gloss: basti (urinary bladder region; standard); door, opening

hindi: यदि बस्तिद्वार पर विपन्न हुई स्त्री की कुक्षि यानी पेट फड़के,
english: If the kukṣi (belly) of a woman who has perished at the bastidvāra (door of the basti) quivers,
notes: GROUPING: the sentence is completed in unit 144. "Perished" (vipanna) means ruined or dead; the context (extracting the child) suggests death but the line does not say so. "Bastidvāra" is not explained in the line (the opening of the bladder region or the pelvic outlet are possible); read literally. Kukṣi = belly or abdomen, not specifically the womb.

hindi: जन्म के समय तब शीघ्र चीरकर शिशु को निकाले।
english: At the time of birth, then, quickly having split (it) open, one should take out the child.
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete unit 143 (the main clause). The object of pāṭayitvā (the belly, kukṣi) is not stated and is shown as (it). Janmakāle can also be "at the proper time of birth".

words.gloss: payasyā (identity disputed; perhaps vidārī, Indian kudzu, Pueraria tuberosa)

hindi: मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी, शाक यानी सम्भवतः सागौन का बीज, और पयस्या जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द, और सुरदारु यानी सम्भवतः देवदार।
english: Madhuka (probably licorice), the seed of śāka (probably teak), and payasyā (identity disputed; perhaps the Indian kudzu), and suradāru (probably deodar).
notes: Opens the series of seven combinations (145-151), each a half-verse, given with milk (152) in the seven months (153). Śāka may also mean a vegetable; "teak" is the usual identification in drug lists (probable). Madhuka = licorice (probable; the tree Madhuca is the other possible plant). Payasyā: disputed (vidārī and other milky climbers are named). Suradāru and devadāru are both deodar. The verb "should apply" is in unit 153.

words.gloss: aśmantaka (identity disputed; perhaps the apta tree, Bauhinia racemosa)

hindi: अश्मन्तक जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सम्भवतः आपटा, काले तिल, ताम्रवल्ली जिसकी पहचान अस्पष्ट है, और शतावरी।
english: Aśmantaka (identity disputed; perhaps the apta tree), black sesame seeds, tāmravallī (the copper-coloured creeper; identity unclear) and śatāvarī (wild asparagus).
notes: Second combination. Aśmantaka: disputed (Bauhinia racemosa or a fig, Ficus species). Tāmravallī: literally "copper creeper", no standard identification here (unidentified); a synonym of another climber is possible. Kṛṣṇatila = black sesame (standard).

words.gloss: with; utpala (blue water lily; probable); sārivā

hindi: वृक्षदनी यानी सम्भवतः बांदा, पयस्या जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, लता जिसकी पहचान अस्पष्ट है, और उत्पल सहित सारिवा।
english: Vṛkṣadanī (probably the mistletoe vandā), payasyā (identity disputed), latā (a creeper; identity unclear) and sārivā together with utpala (probably blue water lily).
notes: Third combination. Printed sāribā is sārivā (b/v interchange in this print, recorded once; no flag). The division latā | sotpalasārivā is chosen; the alternative is latā sotpalā | sārivā ("latā with utpala, and sārivā"). Latā alone is a generic word for creeper and no identification is made. Utpala may also be a different lotus; blue water lily is the usual reading (probable).

words.gloss: anantā (identity disputed; in some sources a synonym of sārivā)
rāsnā (identity disputed; on a conjectural reading of printed rāstrā)
padmā (lotus, or a plant named padmā; unclear)

hindi: अनन्ता जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सारिवा, अनुमानित पाठ पर रास्ना जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, पद्मा यानी कमल या इसी नाम की कोई वनस्पति, और मधुयष्टिका यानी मुलेठी।
english: Anantā (identity disputed; sometimes the same as sārivā), sārivā, rāsnā (on a conjectural reading of the printed rāstrā; identity disputed), padmā (lotus, or a plant so named; unclear) and madhuyaṣṭikā (licorice).

text_flags.why: possible: rāsnā is the drug name; stra for sna as in unit 124

notes: Fourth combination. Anantā and sārivā are both listed, so they are taken as separate drugs here. Padmā: the lotus, or padmaka (a different plant) — unclear. Madhuyaṣṭikā = licorice (standard).

words.gloss: the two bṛhatīs (large and small nightshade, bṛhatī and kaṇṭakārī; probable)

hindi: बृहतीद्वय यानी बड़ी और छोटी कटेरी, काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी, क्षीरी वृक्षों की शुंग यानी कोंपलों की छाल और घी।
english: The two bṛhatīs (the large and small nightshade, probably), kāśmarya (gambhārī), the bark of the shoots (śuṅga) of milk-yielding trees (kṣīrin), and ghṛta (ghee).
notes: Fifth combination. Bṛhatī-dvaya = bṛhatī plus kaṇṭakārī (probable). Kṣīri-śuṅga-tvacaḥ is a compound that can be read "bark of the shoots of milk-yielding trees" (taken here) or as three separate items (milk-yielding trees, shoots, bark); the trees are not named here (later tradition names four figs; not stated). Kāśmarya = gambhārī (standard). Doubled y in kāśmaryya is a print habit.

words.gloss: madhuparṇikā (identity disputed; perhaps guḍūcī, Tinospora cordifolia, or gambhārī)

hindi: पृश्निपर्णी यानी पिठवन, बला यानी बरियार, शिग्रु यानी सहजन, श्वदंष्ट्रा यानी गोखरू, और मधुपर्णिका जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सम्भवतः गिलोय।
english: Pṛśniparṇī (pithvan), balā (country mallow), śigru (drumstick tree), śvadaṃṣṭrā (puncture-vine), and madhuparṇikā (identity disputed; perhaps giloy).
notes: Sixth combination. Pṛśniparṇī standard. Śvadaṃṣṭrā is usually gokṣura (puncture-vine; probable); kaṇṭakārī has also been called by this name. Madhuparṇikā is disputed (guḍūcī, gambhārī or others).

words.gloss: kaseru (a sedge tuber, Scirpus grossus; probable)

hindi: शृंगाटक यानी सिंघाड़ा, बिस यानी कमलनाल, द्राक्षा यानी अंगूर, कसेरु यानी सम्भवतः कसेरू नामक कन्द, मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और सिता यानी सम्भवतः मिश्री।
english: Śṛṅgāṭaka (water chestnut), bisa (lotus stalk), drākṣā (grape), kaseru (probably the sedge tuber of that name), madhuka (probably licorice) and sitā (probably white sugar).
notes: Seventh combination. Sitā literally "white"; sugar is the usual sense in lists (probable). Bisa = lotus rhizome or stalk (standard).

hindi: ये सभी योग दूध के साथ, जो आधे श्लोक पर समाप्त होते हैं।
english: All these combinations (yoga) with milk, those that end at a half-verse.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in unit 153, which supplies the verb yojayet. "Ardhaślokasamāpana" = ending at (completed within) a half-verse: each combination fills one half-verse (145-151). The printed sarvaitān is sarvān etān.

hindi: क्रम से सात महीनों में गर्भ के बहने यानी गर्भस्राव होने पर प्रयोग करे।
english: In sequence, in the seven months, when the fetus is flowing (miscarrying), one should apply (them).
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete units 145-152 (the verb for the combinations). "Garbhe sravati" is a locative absolute: with the fetus flowing, i.e. garbhasrāva (miscarriage; probable). The object "them" is the combinations of 152 and is shown as (them). Seven combinations match seven months.

words.gloss: kapittha (wood-apple, Limonia acidissima; standard); bilva (bael, Aegle marmelos; standard); bṛhatī; paṭola (pointed gourd, Trichosanthes dioica; standard); ikṣu (sugarcane, Saccharum officinarum; standard); nidigdhikā (kaṇṭakārī, Solanum virginianum; standard)

hindi: कपित्थ यानी कैथ, बिल्व यानी बेल, बृहती यानी बड़ी कटेरी, पटोल यानी परवल, इक्षु यानी ईख और निदिग्धिका यानी कटेरी।
english: Kapittha (wood-apple), bilva (bael), bṛhatī, paṭola (pointed gourd), ikṣu (sugarcane) and nidigdhikā (kaṇṭakārī, the small nightshade).

text_flags.why: possible: the compound goes with mūlaiḥ in unit 155 (roots of the six); the printed final -n is not needed (16 syllables either way)

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in unit 155 (mūlaiḥ śṛtam …). The printed accusative plural does not fit mūlaiḥ; the sense "with the roots of these" is read, so the final n is treated as a misprint (possible). Kapittha = wood-apple, bilva = bael (glossary). Bṛhatī and nidigdhikā are the large and small nightshades (standard).

hindi: जड़ों से उबाला हुआ दूध महीने में प्रयुक्त करे, और उसी प्रकार आठवें में।
english: One should use milk boiled with roots in the month, and likewise in the eighth.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue unit 154 (the roots of the plants listed there). "Māse" has no ordinal and so is unresolved: it may be a month whose number has dropped out, or "for a month". The print is 16 syllables as it stands, so no dropped word is shown by the metre. The avagraha printed in tathā'ṣṭame (ā + a) is a print habit. Kṣīraṃmāse is divided kṣīram māse.

words.gloss: sārivā; anantā (identity disputed); payasyā (identity disputed); madhuyaṣṭī (licorice)

hindi: नवें में सारिवा, अनन्ता जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, पयस्या जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, और मधुयष्टि यानी मुलेठी के साथ।
english: In the ninth, with sārivā, anantā (identity disputed), payasyā (identity disputed) and madhuyaṣṭī (licorice).
notes: Elliptical: the month noun (māse) and the verb are not stated; yojayet comes in unit 157 and is not supplied here. The milk is understood from 155 but not named in this line. The avagraha printed after ā (sārivā'naṃtā) is a print habit.

hindi: दसवें महीने में पयस्या जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, उससे पकाया हुआ दूध प्रयुक्त करे।
english: In the tenth month one should apply milk cooked with payasyā (identity disputed).
notes: The verb yojayet also serves unit 156 (ninth month). "Siddha" = cooked (glossary). Payasyā: see unit 145.

words.gloss: yaṣṭimadhuka (licorice); nāgara (dry ginger, Zingiber officinale; standard); amaradāru (deodar); with

hindi: अथवा यष्टिमधुक यानी मुलेठी, नागर यानी सोंठ और अमरदारु यानी देवदार के साथ।
english: Or with yaṣṭimadhuka (licorice), nāgara (dry ginger) and amaradāru (deodar).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue unit 157 (the tenth-month milk, cooked with these instead). Amaradāru and devadāru are both deodar (standard). Nāgara = dry ginger (standard).

hindi: इस प्रकार गर्भव्यापत् नामक चौथा अध्याय।
english: Thus the fourth chapter, named Garbhavyāpat (mishap of the fetus).
notes: Colophon. Printed garbhavyāpannāma = garbhavyāpat + nāma (t + n gives n; regular sandhi). Garbhavyāpat: "mishap, calamity (vyāpad) of the fetus (garbha)". The printed caturtho'dhyāyaḥ is caturthaḥ adhyāyaḥ.
